title: RSV Maternal Vaccine Halves Baby Intensive Care Admissions - Medscape

analysis.time: Published 16 August 2026; event period covers winter 2025–2026 and the first full year of the maternal vaccination programme (September 2024–August 2026).
analysis.location_and_population: England, Wales, and Scotland; infants under 6 months of age; pregnant women from 28 weeks gestation.
analysis.event: UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) reports that the national maternal RSV vaccination programme, launched in September 2024, has reduced intensive care admissions among infants under 6 months by about 50% in its first full year.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In the 20 participating NHS trusts, ICU/high-dependency admissions fell from 131 in 2024–2025 to 63 in 2025–2026; peak bronchiolitis attendances were lower and the season shorter; maternal vaccine uptake was 61.7% in England, 56.2% in Wales, and 53.7% in Scotland; earlier UKHSA data showed a single maternal dose provided over 80% protection against hospital admission for newborns.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: UKHSA and NHS confirm programme impact; vaccination programme continues; officials note many thousands of babies remain at risk due to incomplete uptake; RSV season timing shifted from October to early November and peaked in late December 2025; adult RSV vaccination also showed over 40% reduction in hospitalisation among 75–80-year-olds.

analysis.brief_en: The UK’s first full year of a maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination programme has cut intensive care admissions for babies under six months by roughly half, according to figures released by the UK Health Security Agency on 16 August 2026. In the 20 participating NHS trusts, ICU or high-dependency unit admissions for confirmed RSV bronchiolitis fell from 131 in 2024–25 to 63 in 2025–26, while peak emergency attendances were lower and the season shorter. The programme, offered to pregnant women from 28 weeks, achieved uptake of 61.7% in England, 56.2% in Wales, and 53.7% in Scotland. Earlier UKHSA data showed a single maternal dose provided over 80% protection against hospital admission for newborns. Officials also reported a sustained 40% drop in RSV hospitalisations among adults aged 75–80 following routine vaccination. Despite the gains, authorities warned that thousands of infants remain unprotected due to incomplete coverage.

analysis.time: Published 13 August 2026; event period 2025–2026 winter season (March 2025–February 2026) with programme start September 2024.
analysis.location_and_population: United Kingdom; infants under six months admitted to intensive care or high dependency units; pregnant women from 28 weeks gestation; adults aged 75–80 years.
analysis.event: UK Health Security Agency reported a 50% drop in RSV-confirmed ICU admissions among infants under six months during the first full year of a maternal RSV vaccination programme, alongside reduced A&E bronchiolitis attendances and altered seasonal trends.
